findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps full ID lists every batch
findings.body: In CleanAnnotations, CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) routine progress information is logged with r.log.Error, e.g. r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...). These are clearly leftover debug statements: (1) they run at Error level for normal, successful operation, which pollutes error-level logs, dashboards and any alerting on error logs; (2) they log the entire `ids` slice, which can be up to annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size (the test uses 32767) IDs per line, per batch, repeated until the table is clean — megabytes of log spam on a large backlog; (3) the "err" field is always nil at that point because the error was already returned above, so the logs are misleading. These should be removed or downgraded to Debug level without the full ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute without documentation or rationale
findings.body: The cleanup service ticker was changed from time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10) to time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1). This is not mentioned in the PR description, which only describes the annotation delete restructuring. The consequence is that ALL cleanup jobs (expired snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, user invites, short URLs, query history row-limit enforcement, annotation cleanup) now run 10x more often on every Grafana instance, increasing background database load — ironically increasing lock contention with foreground writes, which is the problem this PR is meant to reduce. Combined with the 9-minute per-run timeout in clean(), cleanup work can now effectively run back-to-back. Either this change is unintentional and should be reverted, or it needs to be called out in the PR description and release notes with justification.

findings.title: Placeholder-limit workaround only guards SQLite and keys off config, not actual ID count
findings.body: deleteByIDs special-cases only SQLite (r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999) to inline IDs into the SQL, on the assumption that a DELETE with N `?` placeholders is otherwise safe. Other backends have their own placeholder/statement-size limits (e.g. MySQL prepared statements cap at 65,535 placeholders); with annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size configured above such a limit, every batch of the cleanup job will now fail permanently, whereas the previous subquery-based DELETE worked for any batch size. The guard should be based on len(ids) against per-dialect limits rather than the configured batch size on SQLite only. Also, the comment claims "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" while the new test name states the limit is 32767 for SQLite >= 3.32.0 — the comment and code disagree with the test's stated rationale.

findings.title: Deadlock fix is only exercised on SQLite; no MySQL/Postgres coverage
findings.body: The PR fixes a MySQL-specific deadlock (grafana/grafana#64979), but all tests in this file use db.InitTestDB(t), which defaults to SQLite. The new code paths (fetchIDs + deleteByIDs, the SQLite ID-inlining branch, the batched untilDoneOrCancelled loop) are only validated against SQLite semantics; in particular the inline-ID branch at deleteByIDs is exercised only via the SQLite test, and no test verifies that the split statements actually avoid the deadlock under concurrent inserts on MySQL. There is also no test for the non-SQLite placeholder path with a large batch size. A MySQL integration test (or at least a concurrency test simulating interleaved inserts during cleanup) is needed to validate the fix the PR claims to deliver.
